update.title: Separated package histories with VCSH
update.summary: Constellation now uses VCSH to track packages independently inside one shared workspace, giving every package a formal Git ownership boundary without splitting apart the files that work together.
update.previewAlt: An isometric shared workspace platform with distinct package modules connected to separate external history archives.

blocks.body:
## Track one workspace package by package

Constellation Framework keeps related tools and services together in one filesystem so they can share integrations and be worked on as a connected environment. A single repository would combine unrelated package histories, while nested repositories would introduce Git boundaries throughout the workspace.

VCSH keeps repository metadata outside the package tree and lets each repository track selected paths inside the shared worktree. A package can stay exactly where the rest of the workspace expects it while retaining its own commits, branches, and remotes.

blocks.caption: External VCSH repositories assign independent history and ownership to package paths inside one shared Constellation worktree.

  subgraph Workspace[Shared Constellation worktree]

    PackageB[Package B paths]
  end

blocks.body:
## Make repository ownership explicit

Each package now has a defined VCSH repository identity, repository conventions, and ignore rules. Git operations can target that identity instead of inferring ownership from whichever directory happens to be active.

This formalizes tracking across the workspace: changes can be found across packages, assigned to the repository that owns them, and committed without pulling neighboring package work into the same history. The structure now covers 53 packages, including 10 forks with their own upstream configuration.

part_of.title: Built a discovery-based registry for a software workspace
part_of.summary: Each tool and service now carries its own manifest, letting the workspace discover package identity, status, interfaces, runtime, and dependencies directly from package directories.

related.title: Made Work Report Git tracking package-aware
related.summary: Work Report now uses the report’s project identity as the repository context for commit metadata, diff statistics, and captured Git evidence, routing VCSH-backed packages through their independent histories.
